preliminary.checked_obligation: Verify that the witness x=ε^(1/N) establishes that (f_n) does not converge uniformly on [0,1].
preliminary.reason: The witness calculation is correct only after defining the pointwise limit f by f(x)=0 for x<1 and f(1)=1: then x=ε^(1/N)<1 and |f_N(x)-f(x)|=ε. The proof does not define or establish this limit, nor state that any uniform limit must equal the pointwise limit. The supplied group-theoretic rules are inapplicable to this topology problem.
unresolved_conditions: Define f(x)=0 for 0≤x<1 and f(1)=1, and verify that f_n converges pointwise to f.
Explain that uniform convergence would imply convergence to this same pointwise limit, so a fixed ε∈(0,1) and the stated witness for every N contradict uniform convergence.

problem.theorem: Define $f_{n}:[0,1] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ by the equation $f_{n}(x)=x^{n}$. Show that the sequence $\left(f_{n}\right)$ does not converge uniformly.

target_node.claim: Asserts nonuniform convergence using the witness $x=\varepsilon^{1/N}$ and the equality $d(f_N(x),f(x))=\varepsilon$.
target_node.text:
\begin{proof}

    The sequence $\left(f_n\right)_n$ does not converge uniformly, since given $0<\varepsilon<1$ and $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$, for $x=\varepsilon^{1 / N}$ we have $d\left(f_N(x), f(x)\right)=\varepsilon$.
